note: Machine-managed lore registry. Edit via `uv run python -m tools lore domain add|relation add`, never by hand. Domains are the unit of parallel ownership: one legion owns one bible/<domain>.jsonl exclusively. Edges are sharded per authoring batch so two agents never write the same file.

cosmology.blurb: The multiverse itself: universes, the layers between them, world laws and how they bind, Dao and its per-world variations, metaphysical concepts, and supernatural phenomena. Everything else ultimately descends from this file, so contradictions here propagate everywhere.

worlds.blurb: Individual worlds, planes, pocket dimensions, hidden domains, and destroyed or lost worlds. A world record carries its law composition, life-form ceiling, time flow, upkeep and size band - the authored tier data in game/data/world/tiers is the hard constraint these must respect.

geography.blurb: Continents, regions, mountain ranges, rivers, seas, biomes, climates, spiritual environments and named sites. Geography is the slowest-changing cause in the chain World Laws -> Environment -> Resources -> Cultivation -> Civilization -> Character.

ecology.blurb: Mundane and supernatural ecosystems, flora, fauna, spirit creatures and environmental dependencies. A resource that exists must belong to an ecosystem that supports it.

races.blurb: Species, subspecies, bloodlines, hybrids and transformations. Each record covers origin, biology, spiritual nature, lifecycle, environment, society, worldview, history and relationships. A race is NOT a culture, a nation, or a personality.

cultures.blurb: Languages, customs, values, etiquette, clothing, cuisine, art, architecture, festivals, marriage, death rites and taboos. Cultures are held by communities, not by species: one race must sustain several cultures and one culture must admit several races.

civilizations.blurb: Nations, kingdoms, empires, city-states, settlements, governments, legal systems, economies, infrastructure and trade networks. A civilization exists because of material and historical causes, never because the setting needs one.

organizations.blurb: Sects, clans, guilds, academies, armies, merchant organizations, criminal networks and secret societies. Every organization must state what it is for, what it spends, and what happens to its members who leave.

families.blurb: Families, lineages, marriage networks, inheritance, reputation, internal politics, blood feuds and generational ambition. Distinct from organizations: a family is a kinship, an organization is a purpose.

cultivation.blurb: Cultivation systems, paths, Dao philosophies, techniques, resources, inheritances, teachers, schools and forbidden methods, including regional and per-world variations. A system must be possible under the law composition of the world that hosts it.

religion.blurb: Gods, spirits, faiths, creation myths, philosophical schools, afterlife beliefs and ideological conflict. A religion is a social institution with interests, not only a cosmology.

economy.blurb: Resources, professions, production, currencies, trade, scarcity and economic dependencies. Every war needs an economic cause and every scarce good needs a geography.

politics.blurb: Rulers, offices, claims, diplomacy, treaties, territory, succession, influence and political movements. Position and standing never derive from each other: name who holds an office separately from what anyone thinks of them.

conflicts.blurb: Wars, territorial disputes, ideological conflicts, racial tension, resource competition, revenge cycles, succession struggles and hidden threats. A conflict record must name its economic cause, not only its victor.

history.blurb: Eras, timelines, migrations, discoveries, disasters, collapses and renaissances, plus their unresolved consequences. Chronology lives in attributes (order, span, parents) so the tool can validate a timeline instead of trusting prose.

people.blurb: Founders, rulers, heroes, villains, scholars, cultivators and historically significant individuals. Psychology lives here as attributes: desire, fear, ambition, loyalty, duty, prejudice, trauma and the contradictions between them.

knowledge.blurb: Education, scholarship, technologies, medicine, alchemy, formations, craftsmanship, myths, rumors, propaganda, secrets and restricted knowledge. Knowledge diffuses through contact, so every field states who guards it and who is forbidden it.

mysteries.blurb: Forgotten civilizations, sealed entities, unexplained phenomena, disputed histories and questions deliberately left open. A mystery is a first-class record, not a gap in another record: something can be unknown on purpose.

located_in.blurb: A thing sits inside a larger place or container.

part_of.blurb: Membership in a larger whole that is not primarily spatial.

member_of.blurb: A person or creature belongs to an organization, faction, clan or people.

native_to.blurb: The place a species or people is indigenous to, as opposed to a place it settled in later.

founded_by.blurb: The person or group that established an institution, settlement or tradition.

created_by.blurb: The agent or process that made a thing that was not born, covering artificial life, formations and crafted constructs.

descended_from.blurb: Direct descent: a family from a family, a species from a species, an organization from a dissolved one.

hybrid_of.blurb: Two or more parent lineages combined into one, usually by blood rather than by institution.

originated_from.blurb: The place, event, law or condition a thing came from. The general form of origin; prefer native_to for homeland.

migrated_from.blurb: A people or species that left a homeland and settled elsewhere, normally under pressure.

preceded_by.blurb: Strictly earlier in the same timeline. Use for sequence, not for causation.

caused.blurb: Direct causation. The strongest edge in the book: every event, institution and culture should trace back through several of these.

requires.blurb: A thing cannot exist or function without something else: a cultivation method requires a resource, a ritual requires an event.

depends_on.blurb: Softer than requires: the thing degrades or becomes impractical without the other, but does not stop existing.

controls.blurb: Authority over a place, resource or institution. Distinct from member_of, which is belonging rather than command.

allied_with.blurb: A mutual political or military partnership.

conflicts_with.blurb: Structural opposition over an idea, a resource or a claim, whether or not anyone has taken a field.

trades_with.blurb: Regular material exchange. Every trade edge should be walkable to the geography and the goods that make it possible.

influenced_by.blurb: One thing measurably shaped another without replacing it: a school of thought, an art form, a law.

resembles.blurb: Structural similarity without shared descent. The edge that lets a duplicate concept be recorded honestly instead of being hidden.

believes.blurb: A people, faction or person holds a doctrine, claim or interpretation as true.

knows_about.blurb: A party holds accurate knowledge of a thing. Contrast hidden_from.

hidden_from.blurb: A party is deliberately kept ignorant of a thing that exists.

applies_in.blurb: A law or rule holds force inside a world, tier or jurisdiction. Distinct from located_in: a law is not inside a place, it constrains one.

participated_in.blurb: A person or faction took part in an event, without necessarily favoring its outcome.

opposed_to.blurb: A named individual or house stands against another, as in a blood feud or a personal grudge.
